propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes git-fetch dribble tests to intermittently fail with stall detection when using a shared 2-second timeout window applied to both zero-byte controls and above-floor negative controls.

The test fixture sends rate//10 bytes per 0.1-second wake-up, so delayed scheduler wake-ups reduce cumulative throughput below the configured rate, causing libcurl to abort during long send gaps that would not occur under normal scheduling.
A pure deterministic unit test must prove cumulative bytes-owed calculation equals floor(rate * elapsed) minus bytes already sent after delayed wake-ups.

Zero-byte stall test cases must use the fast 2-second window while one real Git/libcurl integration test must use the production 10-second window to avoid conflating scheduler jitter with actual stall conditions.
